### Reference: runtime internals

#### `CrashPolicy`

class · `import { CrashPolicy } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

The restart rule for supervised processes, one per supervisor, keyed by instance: an asked-for stop or a clean exit
(for `on-failure`) stops; the restart code restarts at once; a crash restarts after `backoff`, doubling with each
crash in the last hour, and more than `maxPerHour` crashes in an hour gives up (the caller may roll back).

```ts
class CrashPolicy {
  constructor(options: CrashPolicyOptions);
  /** Decide what follows `exit` of the instance `key`, run under `policy`; `stopping` when the stop was asked for. */
  decide(key: string, policy: RestartPolicy, exit: Pick<ProcessExit, "code">, stopping: boolean): ExitDecision;
  /** Forget an instance's crashes (after a rollback, a new version or an uninstall). */
  forget(key: string): void;
}
```

#### `CrashPolicyOptions`

interface · `import { CrashPolicyOptions } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

How `CrashPolicy` decides.

```ts
interface CrashPolicyOptions {
  /** The longest wait between restarts (`HARNESS_SUPERVISE_BACKOFF_MAX`). */
  readonly maxWait: number;
  /** The exit code that asks for an immediate restart (`RESTART_CODE` unless the supervisor sets another). */
  readonly restartCode: number;
  readonly clock?: (() => number) | undefined;
}
```

#### `ExitDecision`

type · `import { ExitDecision } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

What to do after a process exits.

```ts
type ExitDecision =
| { readonly action: 'stopped' }
| { readonly action: 'restart-now' }
| { readonly action: 'restart'; readonly wait: number; readonly crashes: number }
| { readonly action: 'give-up'; readonly crashes: number };
```

#### `AccessDeniedReader`

class · `import { AccessDeniedReader } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

Reads a child's output for the errors Node's permission model throws (`code: 'ERR_ACCESS_DENIED'` with its
`permission` and `resource` fields, as an uncaught error prints them), so a supervisor can report the refusal.

```ts
class AccessDeniedReader {
  /** Feed one line; returns the refusal once its error has been read through. */
  line(line: string): AccessDenied | undefined;
}
```

interface · `import { AccessDenied } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

```ts
}
```

#### `AllowlistProxy`

class · `import { AllowlistProxy } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

An HTTP proxy on 127.0.0.1 that lets through only allowed hosts: `CONNECT` tunnels for https, forwarding for http.

```ts
class AllowlistProxy implements NetworkGate {
  constructor(options: AllowlistProxyOptions);
  /** Listen on a free port of 127.0.0.1; resolves to the proxy's URL. */
  start(): Promise<string>;
  setAllowed(allow: readonly string[]): void;
  /** Stop listening and cut every open tunnel. */
  close(): Promise<void>;
}
```

#### `AllowlistProxyOptions`

interface · `import { AllowlistProxyOptions } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

What an allowlist proxy lets through, and who hears of what it refuses.

```ts
interface AllowlistProxyOptions {
  /** The hosts let through at first (`grants.network`, plus the hub's own); `setAllowed` changes them. */
  readonly allow: readonly string[];
  readonly onRefused: (refusal: ProxyRefusal) => void;
}
```

#### `NETWORK_GUARD`

const · `import { NETWORK_GUARD } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

What a supervised child preloads to hold its sockets to its proxy and the hub. `--require`, not `--import`: a preload
runs before a loader's `--import`, so Node strips the guard's types itself, and the loader still registers after it.


#### `NetworkGate`

interface · `import { NetworkGate } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

A child's network gate: listens, can change what it lets through, and is closed once the child is gone.

```ts
interface NetworkGate {
  /** Start listening; resolves to the proxy URL the child is pointed at. */
  start(): Promise<string>;
  /** Let through `allow` from now on (the grant changed while the child runs); tunnels already open stay. */
  setAllowed(allow: readonly string[]): void;
  close(): Promise<void>;
}
```

#### `McpFace`

class · `import { McpFace } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

The system's native fns as MCP tools, with its resources and commands beside them, and the server and transport that offer them.

```ts
class McpFace implements McpToolSource {
  /** `contexts` fills the system's commands as prompts (the system runtime). */
  constructor(table: SystemTable, env: RunEnvironment, version: string, limits: McpLimits, contexts: ContextTexts);
  /** The MCP server (JSON-RPC: `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/*`, and `resources/*` and `prompts/*` when the system has them). */
  get server(): McpServer;
  /** The tools offered now. */
  tools(): McpTool[];
  /** Run the fn behind a tool; `undefined` when there is no such tool. */
  call(name: string, args: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<McpToolResult | undefined>;
  /** Fns added or removed at runtime change the tool list. */
  onChange(listener: () => void): () => void;
  /** Serve over stdin/stdout or Streamable HTTP. Resolves once listening (stdio serves until stdin ends). */
  serve(how: McpServe): Promise<void>;
  close(): Promise<void>;
}
```

Refers to: [`Json`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.primitives-ts#core-json).

#### `LlmWire`

class · `import { LlmWire } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

aeye → wire for the parts where callers differ in what the wire can't carry.

```ts
class LlmWire {
  constructor(options: LlmWireOptions);
  /** An aeye message as it crosses the wire or is saved. Provider caches and reasoning details stay behind. */
  message(message: Message): LlmMessage;
  /** An aeye request as JSON: zod schemas become JSON schema; an empty tool list is left out. */
  request(request: Request): LlmRequest;
  /** A zod schema as JSON schema (its input side). */
  jsonSchema(schema: z.ZodType): Json;
}
```

Refers to: [`Json`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.primitives-ts#core-json), [`LlmRequest`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.llm-ts#core-llmrequest).

#### `LlmWireOptions`

interface · `import { LlmWireOptions } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

How `LlmWire` treats what the wire can't carry.

```ts
interface LlmWireOptions {
  /**
   * `refuse` throws a `LinkGap`, for requests that will be sent on (a lossy request would reach the model changed).
   * `placeholder` keeps going, for records: a schema part becomes `{}` (any value) and an unsendable part's content
   * becomes `[binary content]`.
   */
  readonly unrepresentable: 'refuse' | 'placeholder';
}
```

#### `RedirectOptions`

interface · `import { RedirectOptions } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

How `followRedirects` fetches.

```ts
interface RedirectOptions {
  /** The fetch underneath; it is always called with `redirect: 'manual'`. */
  readonly fetch: FetchFn;
  /** Checked before every hop is requested; throws to refuse it. */
  check(url: URL, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<void>;
  /** The most redirects followed. */
  readonly redirects: number;
  readonly problems: RedirectProblems;
}
```

#### `RedirectProblems`

interface · `import { RedirectProblems } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

The errors a redirect chain fails with, so each caller names them its own way.

```ts
interface RedirectProblems {
  /** A redirect without a location that parses against `at`. */
  noLocation(at: URL): unknown;
  /** More than `limit` redirects from `start`. */
  tooMany(start: URL, limit: number): unknown;
  /** What to throw when the fetch at `at` threw `error` (default: `error` itself). */
  failed?(error: unknown, at: URL): unknown;
}
```
